properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RC4/RC4Drop module of the vendored CryptoJS 3.1.9-1 bundle shipped inside the wallet UI. Library API surface — CryptoJS.RC4 is never invoked by application code (only docstring examples inside the bundle). The image ships the algorithm; that is the inventory question.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TripleDES module of the vendored CryptoJS bundle shipped in the wallet UI (Sweet32-class 64-bit block cipher). Library API surface; no app call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 module shipped with the wallet twice: as the npm crypto-js dependency used by the main-process PoW chain, and compiled into the UI's vendored crypto bundle. Changeable here (strip unused CryptoJS modules at build time); no live MD5 use found in the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 ships to users inside the vendored crypto-js bundle (module 27 of ui/js/iota.crypto.js); the app never calls CryptoJS.SHA1 directly — the only in-bundle consumer of crypto-js hashing is Kerl, which rides on algo.SHA3. Presence is the inventory question; a reachable surface via window.IOTACrypto/CryptoJS globals.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-MD5 helper in the vendored CryptoJS bundle shipped with the wallet UI. Library surface; no app call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Build-toolchain dependency inventory entry: bcrypt-pbkdf (bcrypt-style PBKDF) reaches only the electron-builder/dev chain via sshpk's OpenSSH-key parsing. Not shipped in the wallet runtime; quantum relevance of the KDF is nil in this position.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Digest comparisons in client-side history display logic. Practice note only: the digests are real IOTA bundle/transaction hashes, but the comparisons run on the user's own data in the local renderer; a timing leak is not exploitable from outside. Kept as a constant-time-comparison practice item.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev/build-time transitive dependency of the packaging toolchain (request → http-signature → sshpk → tweetnacl), not linked into the shipped wallet runtime (runtime deps: curl.lib.js, ffi, fs-extra, glob...). tweetnacl@0.14.5 provides Ed25519; recorded for the dependency inventory — presence is the question, urgency is decided downstream.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same tweetnacl@0.14.5 chain (sshpk/bcrypt-pbkdf, dev-only, packaging toolchain); provides X25519 scalar-multiplication key agreement. Not used by the wallet runtime; recorded for the dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: IOTA Foundation Reclaim Service public key (reclaim@iota.org), v4 PGP public-key packet, RSA-4096, created 2017-10-31, hardcoded at ui/js/ui.recover.js:11 (IF_RECLAIM_SERVICE_PUB_KEY). Its one use: the October-2017 reclaim/recovery tool — ui.recover.js:493 openpgp.encrypt (provider: openpgp.js ^2.5.12, bower dep declared with a typo'd source name 'opengpg' at ui/bower.json:19, loaded ui/index.html:15). The flow at ui.recover.js:390-393 encrypts data = oldSeed + ',' + proofAddress + ',' + pepper

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Configuration asset, not the sponge itself: the flag exists so post-October-2017 funds are handled with Kerl while legacy flows can still run on Curl. The actual Keccak-384 sponge instantiation is ui/js/iota.crypto.js:907-909 (CryptoJS.algo.SHA3.create(); init({outputLength: 384})) — not covered by any roster site, so reported as a separate finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped library surface in the UI bundle. No first-party call site invokes it (CryptoJS referenced nowhere outside iota.crypto.js). Dangerous defaults if ever called: crypto-js 3.1.9 PBKDF2 cfg = {keySize: 128/32, hasher: SHA1, iterations: 1} (iota.crypto.js:6519-6522) — one iteration; the bundle also ships EvpKDF (MD5-based, 1 iteration) behind AES passphrase mode.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Strong-MAC surface (HmacSHA256/384/512) available in the vendored CryptoJS bundle shipped with the wallet UI. No application call site found; presence is the inventory question.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES module shipped with the wallet via crypto-js (production PoW chain) and compiled into the UI bundle. Notably, the wallet performs NO local encryption: the seed lives only in renderer memory (connection.seed) and is never persisted or CryptoJS-encrypted. Changeable here (strip unused modules).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl's authenticated encryption (secretbox/box), available through the same dev-only packaging-toolchain chain. Presence recorded; not exercised by wallet runtime code in this tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-toolchain crypto library declaration. tweetnacl 0.14.5's primitives (X25519, Ed25519 — Shor-vulnerable) are recorded as their own package-lock objects by the deterministic pass; this object is the library-level entry for them. Not shipped in the wallet runtime.
